signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew vs Carry Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.70, anchored firmly below its SMA20 at 157.36, SMA50 at 159.54, and SMA200 at 158.40. A massive 264bp OIS carry advantage via SOFR 3.62% vs TONA 0.98% keeps the fundamental backdrop tilted toward the dollar, while Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% reflects a 275bp policy spread. However, the options market exhibits an aggressive downside hedge, with 1M 25d risk reversal printing at −1.95 put skew alongside ATM IV matched to HV30 at 9.8%. This deep put premium directly conflicts with speculative positioning, where COT leveraged funds remain net short JPY by −53,255 contracts despite a sharp +58,042 WoW short-covering surge. The options market is actively pricing elevated downside tail risk into the upcoming BoJ and FOMC decisions, overriding the structural carry bid. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY, downside protection pricing dominates carry backdrop. Catalyst: Fed interest rate decision 16 Sep followed by BoJ decision 18 Sep. Risk: A hawkish FOMC delivery drives spot above the 157.36 SMA20 resistance, forcing options skew to normalize.

signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard registers a decisive bilateral theme, with USD leading all peers at +0.517% across 9 pairs while SEK lags at −0.596% across 2 pairs, producing a 1.113% spread. USD/SEK spot trades at 9.747, positioned cleanly above its SMA20 at 9.564, SMA50 at 9.591, and SMA200 at 9.349. Macro fundamentals strongly reinforce this divergence: Fed policy at 3.75% holds a 200bp nominal rate advantage over the Riksbank at 1.75%, while US real policy rates sit at +1.35% versus Sweden's mildly accommodative −0.32%. Furthermore, Sweden's Economic Surprise Index print of −29.2 highlights persistent domestic macro misses compared to a stable US ESI at 0.0. The divergence reflects systemic divergence in monetary policy stance and domestic growth momentum. Trade bias: Long USD/SEK, policy and growth divergence favor bilateral extension. Catalyst: FOMC statement and rate decision 16 Sep. Risk: A dovish FOMC outcome or unexpected Riksbank hawkish turn compresses the G10 spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning Exhaustion
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7133, holding below its SMA20 at 0.7170 while remaining above the SMA50 at 0.7073 and SMA200 at 0.7006. CFTC data shows leveraged funds holding +48,379 net long contracts, putting speculative positioning at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +1.72. That crowded long profile is experiencing initial fatigue, reflected in a weekly contraction of −1,871 contracts while 1M 25d risk reversals display a moderate −0.78 put skew. Although the RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% provides a 60bp policy carry advantage and AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.62% yields a 73bp OIS advantage, the extreme long crowding limits further upside. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, crowded speculative long vulnerable to unwinding. Catalyst: FOMC rate decision 16 Sep. Risk: A decisive close above the 0.7170 SMA20 resistance with fresh institutional buying invalidates the exhaustion read.

signals.title: GBP/USD — CPI Event Risk vs Options Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3489, testing immediate support at its SMA50 at 1.3481 and holding above the SMA200 at 1.3454 while capped beneath the SMA20 at 1.3559. Leveraged funds hold an elevated long exposure of +40,361 contracts at the 86th percentile of the 52-week range, though positioning has trimmed by −7,143 contracts over the past week. Ahead of the high-impact UK August CPI release, implied volatility runs at 5.4% against a realized HV30 of 3.6%, reflecting an elevated 1.8-point vol risk premium. While BoE and Fed policy rates remain level at 3.75%, SONIA at 3.73% yields a negligible 11bp carry advantage over SOFR at 3.62%. Elevated event volatility pricing and speculative trimming suggest vulnerability to negative inflation surprises. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD, downside vulnerability into heavy UK event risk. Catalyst: UK August CPI release 16 Sep 06:00 UTC (consensus 2.5% YoY). Risk: UK CPI exceeds consensus significantly, prompting aggressive BoE rate hike pricing and driving spot through 1.3559.
